analysis.investment_thesis: Angel One built a spectacular retail broking franchise growing profits at 46% CAGR over nine years, but SEBI's F&O regulations have broken the growth story — net profit fell from INR 1,172 Cr (FY25) to INR 915 Cr (FY26), and borrowings have ballooned from INR 788 Cr (FY23) to INR 7,951 Cr (FY26). When the story changes this fast, I walk away.
key_strengths: Long-term track record is exceptional: revenue CAGR 31%, profit CAGR 46% over nine years with a scalable tech platform (Angel One Super App)
Forward P/E of 20x and P/E of 32x are reasonable on historical earnings — not outrageously priced for what was a fast grower
Strong FII + DII institutional ownership (30%+ combined) signals professional validation of the business model
key_risks: SEBI's F&O restrictions directly impair Angel One's highest-margin revenue stream — this is regulatory risk hitting the core business, not a temporary headwind
Borrowings exploded from INR 788 Cr (FY23) to INR 7,951 Cr (FY26) as the margin funding book scaled — D/E of 0.76 and rising breaches my 0.6 threshold
Operating cash flow has been deeply negative for three consecutive years: -INR 330 Cr (FY24), -INR 1,860 Cr (FY25), -INR 4,142 Cr (FY26) — the business is consuming cash at an alarming rate
red_flags: EARNINGS ARE DECLINING: net profit down 22% YoY in FY26 — my cardinal rule is that decelerating growth kills stocks, and this is outright contraction
Revenue also dipped from INR 5,239 Cr to INR 5,137 Cr — the story of a high-growth tech platform no longer holds at current data points
Finance costs surged to INR 437 Cr in FY26 (up 48% YoY) while net profit fell — the leverage is working against shareholders, not for them
analysis.detailed_analysis: Angel One is a classic example of what I warn against: a great business whose story has changed. For years this was one of India's best growth stories — a tech-first broker democratising markets. I would have loved it at a PEG under 1.0x in FY22-23. But SEBI's regulatory actions on F&O trading have structurally altered the revenue mix, and the numbers confirm it: profits fell 22% in FY26 while borrowings surged 133%. When earnings go from growing at 46% to shrinking at 22%, the market will re-rate the P/E multiple down, not up — a double hit of falling earnings and compression. The negative OCF pattern is particularly alarming; the business is funding its margin lending book through external debt, and finance costs are now the fastest-growing line item. Until I see two consecutive quarters of profit recovery and stabilising borrowings, this is a stock I avoid entirely.
